openshift_diagnostics_guide.overview:
Comprehensive guide for using OpenShift CLI (oc) commands to investigate cluster state, diagnose infrastructure issues, and correlate cluster events with application performance problems identified in Instana. This guide covers systematic approaches to pod troubleshooting, resource analysis, and configuration validation.
CRITICAL USAGE RESTRICTION: OpenShift commands should ONLY be used when performing ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS.
When to use OpenShift diagnostics: - User explicitly asks to "analyze root cause" or "investigate incident" - Correlating infrastructure state with Instana findings during RCA - Investigating pod crashes, OOMKills, or deployment issues as part of RCA
When NOT to use OpenShift diagnostics: - User asks for metrics → Use Instana (manage_applications, analyze_infrastructure) - User asks for services → Use Instana (manage_applications with resource_type="metrics") - User asks for application data → Use Instana MCP tools - General queries about system state → Use Instana first
The workflow is: Instana identifies symptoms → OpenShift correlates infrastructure state

category.name: pod_health_investigation
category.description: Commands to assess pod status, lifecycle, and health

command.name: list_pods
command.purpose: Get overview of all pods with status, restarts, and node placement

key_columns.column: How long pod has been running
Which node the pod is running on

red_flags.flag: READY: 0/1 or not all containers ready

command.name: describe_pod
command.purpose: Get detailed pod information including events, conditions, and container states

section.name: Events
section.description: Recent events affecting the pod (last hour by default)
section.look_for: - FailedScheduling: Resource constraints, node selector issues - Unhealthy: Failed liveness/readiness probes - BackOff: Container startup failures - Killing: Pod termination events - FailedMount: Volume mounting issues - FailedAttachVolume: PVC attachment problems

section.name: Conditions
section.description: Pod lifecycle conditions (PodScheduled, Initialized, Ready, ContainersReady)
section.look_for: - Ready: False (pod not ready to serve traffic) - ContainersReady: False (containers not healthy) - Reason and Message fields explain why

section.name: Container States
section.description: Current state of each container (Running, Waiting, Terminated)
section.look_for: - State: Waiting with Reason: CrashLoopBackOff - Last State: Terminated with Exit Code (non-zero = error) - Exit Code 137: OOMKilled (out of memory) - Exit Code 1: General application error

section.name: Resource Requests/Limits
section.description: CPU and memory requests and limits
section.look_for: - Limits too low (causing OOMKills) - Requests too high (causing scheduling issues) - No limits set (risk of resource exhaustion)

command.name: get_pod_yaml
command.purpose: Get complete pod specification in YAML format
command.when_to_use: When you need to examine: - Environment variables and their sources - Volume mounts and configurations - Security context settings - Init containers - Annotations and labels

command.name: list_pods_by_label
command.purpose: Filter pods by labels (e.g., app=payment-service)

category.name: log_analysis
category.description: Commands to retrieve and analyze container logs

command.name: get_logs
command.purpose: Get logs from a pod's container

options.option: Show logs from previous container instance (after crash)

pattern.name: error_detection
pattern.search_for: - ERROR, FATAL, SEVERE keywords - Exception stack traces - "Connection refused", "Timeout", "Unable to connect" - "OutOfMemoryError", "StackOverflowError" - HTTP 5xx status codes

pattern.name: performance_issues
pattern.search_for: - Slow query warnings - Thread pool exhaustion messages - GC pause time warnings - Connection pool exhaustion - Circuit breaker state changes

pattern.name: configuration_errors
pattern.search_for: - "Configuration error", "Invalid configuration" - Missing environment variables - Failed to load properties/config files - Authentication/authorization failures

example.description: Get logs from last hour with timestamps

command.name: logs_from_all_pods
command.purpose: Get logs from all pods matching a label selector
command.use_case: Useful when investigating issues across multiple replicas of a service

category.name: event_investigation
category.description: Commands to examine cluster events and changes

command.name: get_events
command.purpose: List recent events in the namespace

options.option: Watch for new events in real-time

event.reason: Insufficient CPU/memory, node selector mismatch, taints/tolerations
event.action: Check node resources and pod resource requests
Check probe configuration and application health endpoint

event.reason: Container failed to start, crashing repeatedly
event.action: Check container logs and exit codes

event.reason: Unable to mount volume (PVC not bound, wrong permissions)
event.action: Check PVC status and storage class
Check if reason is OOMKilled, review memory limits

command.name: events_for_pod
command.purpose: Get events specific to a particular pod

category.name: resource_utilization
category.description: Commands to check CPU, memory, and resource usage

command.name: top_pods
command.purpose: Show current CPU and memory usage for pods

interpretation.metric: - Compare to CPU requests/limits - High CPU (near limit) = potential throttling - Consistently high = may need more resources
- Compare to memory requests/limits - Near limit = risk of OOMKill - Steadily increasing = potential memory leak

command.name: top_nodes
command.purpose: Show current CPU and memory usage for nodes
command.interpretation: - High CPU/memory percentage = node under pressure - May cause pod evictions or scheduling issues - Check if specific nodes are overloaded

command.name: describe_node
command.purpose: Get detailed node information including capacity, allocatable resources, and conditions

section.name: Conditions
section.look_for: - MemoryPressure: True (node running out of memory) - DiskPressure: True (node running out of disk space) - PIDPressure: True (too many processes) - Ready: False (node not healthy)

section.name: Allocated resources
section.look_for: - CPU/Memory requests as percentage of capacity - High allocation (>80%) = scheduling constraints

section.name: Non-terminated Pods
section.look_for: - List of pods running on the node - Resource usage per pod

category.name: deployment_investigation
category.description: Commands to examine deployments, replica sets, and rollout status

command.name: get_deployments
command.purpose: List deployments and their replica status

red_flags.flag: UP-TO-DATE less than desired (rollout in progress or stuck)

command.name: describe_deployment
command.purpose: Get detailed deployment information including strategy, conditions, and events

section.name: Replicas
section.look_for: - Desired vs current vs available - Mismatch indicates scaling or rollout issues

section.name: Conditions
section.look_for: - Progressing: False (rollout stuck) - Available: False (no healthy replicas) - ReplicaFailure: True (unable to create replicas)

section.name: Events
section.look_for: - ScalingReplicaSet events - FailedCreate events - Rollout progress messages

command.name: rollout_status
command.purpose: Check the status of a deployment rollout
command.interpretation: - "successfully rolled out" = rollout complete - "Waiting for..." = rollout in progress - Timeout or error = rollout failed

command.name: rollout_history
command.purpose: View deployment revision history
command.use_case: Identify when changes were made and correlate with incidents

command.name: get_replicasets
command.purpose: List replica sets (underlying deployment versions)
command.interpretation: - Multiple ReplicaSets with DESIRED > 0 = rollout in progress - Old ReplicaSets with DESIRED = 0 = previous versions - Check READY vs DESIRED for issues

category.name: configuration_validation
category.description: Commands to examine ConfigMaps, Secrets, and environment configuration

command.name: get_configmap
command.purpose: View ConfigMap contents

validation_checks.check: Check for typos in configuration values
Validate URLs, connection strings, and endpoints

command.name: get_secret
command.purpose: View Secret metadata (values are base64 encoded)
command.note: Secret values are base64 encoded. To decode: echo "[base64-value]" | base64 -d

validation_checks.check: Verify secret exists and is mounted correctly

command.name: list_env_vars
command.purpose: List all environment variables in a pod
command.use_case: Verify environment variables are set correctly, especially those from ConfigMaps and Secrets

category.name: networking_diagnostics
category.description: Commands to investigate service discovery, routing, and connectivity

command.name: get_services
command.purpose: List services and their endpoints

command.name: describe_service
command.purpose: Get detailed service information including endpoints

section.name: Selector
section.look_for: - Verify selector matches pod labels - Mismatch = service won't route to pods

section.name: Endpoints
section.look_for: - List of pod IPs service routes to - Empty endpoints = no healthy pods - Fewer endpoints than expected = some pods not ready

command.name: get_endpoints
command.purpose: View service endpoints (pod IPs)
command.interpretation: - Endpoints list should match ready pods - Empty = no pods passing readiness checks - Changing frequently = pods restarting

command.name: get_routes
command.purpose: List OpenShift routes (external access)

validation_checks.check: Ensure route points to correct service

command.name: describe_route
command.purpose: Get detailed route information

section.name: Service
section.look_for: Service name and port route forwards to

section.name: TLS
section.look_for: TLS termination type and certificate info

category.name: storage_investigation
category.description: Commands to examine persistent volumes and storage

command.name: get_pvc
command.purpose: List Persistent Volume Claims

red_flags.flag: STATUS: Pending (PVC not bound to PV)
STATUS: Lost (PV deleted but PVC remains)

command.name: describe_pvc
command.purpose: Get detailed PVC information including events
command.look_for: - Events showing why PVC is not binding - Storage class availability - Access mode compatibility

step.purpose: Identify pods with high restart counts
Check exit codes and termination reasons
step.look_for: - Exit Code 137 = OOMKilled - Exit Code 1 = Application error - Exit Code 143 = SIGTERM (graceful shutdown)

step.purpose: Check for related events (OOMKilled, Unhealthy, etc.)

step.checks: - Does crash timing match error spikes in Instana? - Are there memory/CPU anomalies before crash? - Are there failed health checks in Instana?

step.purpose: Identify pods with high resource usage
Check resource requests/limits vs actual usage
Check if nodes are under pressure

step.search_for: - GC pause warnings - Slow query logs - Thread pool exhaustion - Connection timeouts

step.checks: - Do slow traces correspond to high CPU/memory pods? - Are there infrastructure bottlenecks? - Is there resource contention?

step.purpose: Check pod status for the deployment

step.checks: - Does deployment timing match incident start? - Are there new errors after deployment? - Did error rates spike after rollout?

step.purpose: Check if pods matching selector are ready
Look for connection errors in logs

step.checks: - Are there connection refused errors in traces? - Do traces show timeouts to specific services? - Are there DNS resolution failures?

guideline.name: timing_correlation
guideline.description: Match OpenShift event timestamps with Instana incident timeline
guideline.technique: - Extract timestamps from oc get events - Compare with Instana incident start time - Look for events within ±5 minutes of incident - Identify causal relationships (event → symptom)

guideline.name: resource_correlation
guideline.description: Match resource metrics between OpenShift and Instana
guideline.technique: - Compare oc top pods with Instana infrastructure metrics - Verify CPU/memory values are consistent - Identify discrepancies (may indicate monitoring gaps) - Look for resource exhaustion patterns

guideline.name: error_correlation
guideline.description: Match error messages between pod logs and Instana traces
guideline.technique: - Extract error messages from oc logs - Search for same errors in Instana traces - Match stack traces to code locations - Identify error propagation paths

guideline.name: deployment_correlation
guideline.description: Correlate deployment changes with incident occurrence
guideline.technique: - Check oc rollout history for recent changes - Compare deployment time with incident start - Look for new errors after deployment - Identify configuration changes in deployment

practice.title: Always check multiple data points
practice.description: Don't rely on a single command. Cross-reference pod status, logs, events, and resource usage to build complete picture.

practice.title: Use appropriate time windows
practice.description: - For active issues: last 1-2 hours of logs/events - For post-incident: 24-48 hours to see patterns - Use --since flag to focus on relevant timeframe

practice.title: Check both current and previous logs
practice.description: Always use --previous flag to see logs from crashed containers, as current logs may not show the failure.

practice.title: Verify configuration consistency
practice.description: Check that ConfigMaps, Secrets, and environment variables match expected values and are consistent across environments.

practice.title: Document command outputs
practice.description: Save command outputs for RCA report. Include timestamps and exact commands used for reproducibility.

issue.name: oomkilled_pods
issue.symptoms: - Pods restarting frequently - Exit code 137 in pod description - "OOMKilled" in events
issue.investigation: - Check memory limits vs actual usage (oc top pods) - Review memory trends in Instana - Look for memory leaks in application logs
issue.typical_causes: - Memory limits too low - Memory leak in application - Unbounded caches or collections - Large object allocations

issue.name: crashloopbackoff
issue.symptoms: - Pod status: CrashLoopBackOff - Increasing restart count - Pod never becomes Ready
issue.investigation: - Check logs with --previous flag - Look at exit codes in pod description - Check for configuration errors - Verify dependencies are available
issue.typical_causes: - Application startup failure - Missing environment variables - Failed database connection - Invalid configuration

issue.name: failed_scheduling
issue.symptoms: - Pod status: Pending - FailedScheduling events - Pod never gets assigned to node
issue.investigation: - Check node resources (oc top nodes) - Review pod resource requests - Check node selectors and taints - Verify PVC binding (if using storage)
issue.typical_causes: - Insufficient cluster resources - Resource requests too high - Node selector mismatch - PVC not bound

issue.name: failed_health_checks
issue.symptoms: - Unhealthy events - Pod not Ready despite Running - Frequent restarts
issue.investigation: - Check liveness/readiness probe configuration - Test health endpoint manually - Review application startup time - Check for slow initialization
issue.typical_causes: - Probe timeout too short - Application slow to start - Health endpoint returning errors - Incorrect probe configuration

issue.name: service_no_endpoints
issue.symptoms: - Service has no endpoints - Connection refused errors - 503 errors from route
issue.investigation: - Check service selector matches pod labels - Verify pods are Ready - Check readiness probe status - Review pod events
issue.typical_causes: - Service selector mismatch - No pods passing readiness checks - Pods not running - Label typo
